newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean prosecutors to seek Hanbo chairman arrest.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean prosecutors to seek Hanbo chairman arrest.

text.p: South Korean state prosecutors said on Thursday they will soon seek the arrest of the chairman of the Hanbo Group, whose steelmaking flagship collapsed in January in a loans scandal.

"Prosecutors questioning Hanbo Chairman Chung Bo-keun have decided to seek an arrest warrant for him," a prosecution official said. Chung's father, Chung Tae-soo, is standing trial for fraud, bribery and other charges linked to South Korea's largest corporate failure.
The official said the state planned to seize more than 300 billion won ($337 million) of Chung family assets so far uncovered.

"Prosecutors are still probing Mr Chung Bo-keun for details needed to charge him for embezzlement," the official said. "Prosecutors will continue to dig further to find out if there is other hidden wealth held by the family."
Hanbo Steel Co, the flagship of South Korea's 14th-biggest industrial conglomerate, collapsed under debts of $5.8 billion.

Chung Tae-soo went on trial this month with nine other people, including a former cabinet minister, after prosecutors uncovered evidence that the loans were obtained after kickbacks to bankers and politicians.
